title: Gojoseon
capsule: Within its own historical span, Gojoseon was ruled by the Wiman (Wei Man) dynasty: the Yan-refugee general Wiman usurped the throne from King Jun around 194 BCE and founded Wiman Joseon at the fortress capital of Wanggeom-seong, near modern Pyongyang. Under Wiman and his successors the kingdom grew wealthy by controlling trade between Han China and the peoples of Manchuria and adopted iron-age military technology. The line ended with Wiman's grandson King Ugeo, whose standoff with Emperor Wu of Han over trade and diplomatic access triggered the Han invasion that captured Wanggeom-seong in 108 BCE — a history wholly separate from the later Joseon dynasty (1392–1897) that shares this entry's Wikidata identifier.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Boundaries are well-attested from the fifteenth century onward through administrative records and border treaties establishing the Yalu and Tumen River frontier with Ming and later Qing China; pre-fifteenth-century northern limits are slightly less precise.
